newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close up, but off early highs.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close up, but off early highs.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly up on Thursday, but off earlier highs, and dealers expected stocks to tread water on Friday.
"It will be largely unaltered tomorrow," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index ended the day up 0.04 point at 128.68, still less than its 128.77 prior to Tuesday's fall and well down from Thursday morning's high of 129.13.
Overall bourse turnover was 782 million crowns. The KFX December future rose 0.15 point, to 128.30, with 378 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Christian Hansen turned in 1995/96 results slightly better than its goal of 10 percent annual growth and fell nine crowns to 770 crowns, where dealers expected it to stay on Friday.
SAS was the most-traded of the top 20 shares, but despite its sharp drop in nine month profits the trade was all sideways and the price remained stuck at 71.50.

Sophus Berendsen continued its recovery after being toppled to 675 crowns following a profits warning on Monday. It edged up a further four crowns on Thursday to close at 708. --Ole Mikkelsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969656
